title: A Close Approximation
statement: Consider all fractions $\frac{p}{q}$ with $p$ and $q$ positive integers, $q \le 200$ and $\frac{p}{q} \ne \frac{7}{19}$. Among the values of these fractions, exactly one is closest to $\frac{7}{19}$. Write this value as $\frac{a}{b}$ in lowest terms, with $a$ and $b$ positive integers. Find $a+b$.
hints: Put $\frac{p}{q} - \frac{7}{19}$ over a common denominator. Look at what values the numerator can take and how the size of $q$ affects the difference.

The difference has size $\frac{|19p-7q|}{19q}$, where the numerator is a positive integer. Use modular arithmetic: reduce modulo $19$ to find which $q$ allow the numerator to equal $1$. The inverse of $7$ modulo $19$ will help.

Since $7 \cdot 11 \equiv 1 \pmod{19}$, a numerator of $1$ requires $q \equiv 8$ or $11 \pmod{19}$. Find the largest such $q \le 200$ and its $p$. A numerator of at least $2$ gives a distance of at least $\frac{2}{19 \cdot 200}$, so compare this with what you found.
solution:
The distance from $\frac{p}{q}$ to $\frac{7}{19}$ is $\frac{N}{19q}$, where $N=|19p-7q|\ge 1$.

If $N=1$ then $7q\equiv\pm1\pmod{19}$. Since $7\cdot 11\equiv 1$, this gives $q\equiv 11$ or $q\equiv 8\pmod{19}$. The largest such $q\le 200$ are $182$ and $198$. For $q=198$, $19p=7\cdot198+1=1387$, so $p=73$, with distance $\frac{1}{19\cdot 198}$.

Any other fraction has either $N=1$ and $q<198$, with distance $\frac{1}{19q}>\frac{1}{19\cdot198}$, or $N\ge 2$, with distance at least $\frac{2}{19\cdot 200}=\frac{1}{19\cdot 100}>\frac{1}{19\cdot198}$.

So the closest value is $\frac{73}{198}$. It is in lowest terms, since a common divisor of $73$ and $198$ divides $19\cdot73-7\cdot198=1$. Hence $a+b=73+198=271$.
